check: P17 §1 instrument check: AIPerf 0.11.0 vs a plain requests client on the same 10 prompts, concurrency 1, OSL 200 with ignore_eos, temperature 0, same NIM container
rule: same order of magnitude; a difference above 20% must be investigated (the rule does not name a statistic)
order: AIPerf first, then the four client runs in the order listed; prefix caching is enabled on the server, so the client runs see a warm prefix cache for these prompts
findings: ITL: all four client runs within 4.3% of AIPerf (-0.2% for the first run). Request latency (e2e): within 4.5%.
TTFT avg: +43.8% and +125.6% in the two localhost client runs (above the 20% rule, investigated); -19.7% and -13.1% in the two 127.0.0.1 runs. TTFT p50: +47.4%, +84.5%, +0.8%, +31.2%.

Investigation: per-request TTFT is bimodal in the client runs: most requests at 17-20 ms (AIPerf min 17.3, p50 17.9 ms) and some at 30-45 ms, plus a slow first request in every run (AIPerf 144 ms; clients 37-267 ms). The minimum TTFT agrees within 1.1% in three runs. The spread moves between runs regardless of connection reuse; 127.0.0.1 reduced it but did not remove it.

Reading: ITL, e2e and the TTFT floor agree; the TTFT differences are 15-25 ms added to some requests on the Python client side of this Windows host and a slow first request, small against the 500 ms and 2000 ms TTFT limits used in P17. At these absolute values (about 18 ms) a 20% rule is a 3.6 ms tolerance.
pass_basis: judged on the agreement of ITL, e2e and the TTFT floor (min, and p50 in the 127.0.0.1 run). TTFT avg/p50 exceeded 20% in some client runs; this verdict is a human judgement written after seeing the data, not a pre-set statistic.
